reference.title: Resistance Band Triceps Pushdown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you push the band down, breathe in as it draws the hands back up.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; choke up on the band or use a stronger one, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower return, choking up on the band (more stretch), then the next band up.

cues.text: Loop a band over a pull-up bar (or a high anchor) and face it, feet hip width, slight forward lean; hold the band palms down about shoulder width, elbows at your sides and bent about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and push the band down until the arms are straight, moving only at the elbows.
Squeeze the back of the arms with the hands in front of the thighs; shoulders down, wrists straight.
Breathe in and let the band draw the hands up slowly until the elbows are back at about 90 degrees; the elbows stay pinned.
Brief pause, keep the trunk still, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows touching your sides; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning over the band to push with body weight
mistakes.fix: Stay nearly upright with a slight lean; move only the forearms.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands up past 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Control the return and stop when the forearms are about level.
Keep the wrists straight in line with the forearms.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees to straight (clinical opinion)
Upper arm along the trunk and still; with the arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018)
Overhand grip about shoulder width on the band (clinical opinion)
Upright or slightly forward, still (clinical opinion)

Anchored high in front so the strands run in front of the face; tension is highest with the arms straight (clinical opinion). Elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights (Andersen 2010)
Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a heavy bench frame or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is lightest at the start and heaviest at the end of the push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Keep the face out of the strands' path in case the band slips off the anchor.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow pain: use a lighter band and a shorter range (clinical opinion).
Wrist discomfort: hold the band with the palms facing each other.
progressions: Stronger band or choke up on it.
Cable pushdown, or an overhead band triceps extension (more triceps growth with the arm overhead in a 12-week study, PubMed 35819335).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the band. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the band. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Holds the upper arm against the side so the elbow stays pinned.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Holds the upper arm against the side so the elbow stays pinned.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so body weight does not push the band.
